judge_point_a_note: * Trust your instincts when you choose.
judge_point_a_beautiful_pose_annotation: How beautiful did the routine look to you?
judge_point_a_flexibility_annotation: How flexible did the body look?
judge_point_a_natural_movement_annotatio: How large and natural were the movements?
judge_point_a_bending_weight_annotation: How powerful did the knee bends and stretches feel?
judge_point_a_jumping_height_annotation: How high were the jumps? (Not the height of the tumbling)
judge_point_a_body_control_annotation: How freely did the gymnast control the body?
judge_point_a_heel_raise_annotation: How high did the gymnast keep the heels?
judge_point_a_weakness_and_strength_anno: How much contrast in speed and strength did you feel?
judge_point_a_connect_movement_annotatio: How smoothly did one movement flow into the next?
judge_point_a_apparatus_control_annotati: How naturally was the apparatus handled?
judge_point_a_music_image_annotation: How well did the routine match the music?
judge_point_a_fine_note: * Use only when none of the five levels above fits.
judge_point_b_dropped_double: Drops of both at the same time
judge_intro_lead_1: On this page you judge a men's rhythmic gymnastics individual routine
judge_intro_lead_emphasis: with the same score sheet the judges use
judge_intro_lead_3: and how it breaks down. Nothing you enter is saved, so try it without worrying.
judge_intro_point_time_body: Just remember the routine you watched and move the sliders. No technical jargon.
judge_intro_point_items_body: The same criteria used in real judging: posture, flexibility, jump height and more.
judge_intro_point_score_body: You see the final score and where every deduction came from. It changes how you watch.
judge_intro_note: You can stop at any point, and start over as often as you like.
judge_step_apparatus_note: Pick the apparatus used in the routine you watched. The page takes on its colour and the score sheet appears.
judge_step_point_a_title: A deductions ─ how the routine was performed
judge_step_point_a_note: Just set eleven sliders between low and high. There is no right answer, so go with your instinct.
judge_step_point_a_waiting: Choose an apparatus and the eleven-item score sheet appears here.
judge_step_point_b_note: Enter how many times the apparatus was dropped and the deductions for other errors. Leave it at 0 if there were none.
judge_step_point_b_waiting: Once the A deductions are set, the fields for drops and errors appear here.
judge_step_score_note: Your score is 10 minus the A and B deductions. The breakdown chart shows where the points went.
judge_step_score_waiting: Once the B deductions are set, the score you gave appears.
judge_before_next_description: Starting from the rules or from routine videos leads to the same place.
judge_result_thanks_1: The score you just saw is your final score.
judge_result_thanks_emphasis: There is no correct score to compare it with.
judge_result_thanks_2: Even for the same routine, judges give slightly different scores. Now follow what your score means.
judge_next_actions_description: It all makes the most sense right after you have given a score.
judge_next_rules_body: The deduction rules are in the rulebook. Compare them with the points you took off and they start to make sense.
judge_next_videos_body: Watch real routines with the same eye. Search by gymnast, team or apparatus.
judge_next_calendar_body: Find the next competition. Dates, venues and whether it is streamed are all listed.
